# Landscape: middle-aged (45–65) job seekers using AI — facts, evidence, tools

Research date: 2026-09-10. Audience assumption: Canadian (Ontario) readers first, US context second. Items marked **[unverified]** or **[secondhand]** could not be confirmed against a primary source in this pass.

---

## 1. The numbers

### Canada (Statistics Canada, Labour Force Survey)
- **Long-term unemployment (27+ weeks) share of all unemployed:** 22.8% (Feb 2026), 22.5% (Apr 2026), **24.0% of ~1.5M unemployed (Aug 2026)** — vs. a 2017–2019 pre-pandemic average of 17.1%. [StatCan Daily, Aug 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260904/dq260904a-eng.htm); [Apr 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260508/dq260508a-eng.htm); [Feb 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260313/dq260313a-eng.htm)
- **Unemployment rate, 55+:** 5.1% (Dec 2025), 4.9% (Feb–Mar 2026), 5.2% (Jun 2026, when employment among 55+ fell −47,000 / −1.1%). Lower than the all-ages rate, but the headline rate hides duration. [Mar 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260410/dq260410a-eng.htm); [Jun 2026](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260710/dq260710a-eng.htm); [Dec 2025](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260109/dq260109a-eng.htm)
- **Duration by age (55–64, 65+), including 27+ weeks and average weeks:** in StatCan **Table 14-10-0342-01** ("Duration of unemployment, monthly, seasonally adjusted"), which has age breakdowns. Pull the live figure when writing: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1410034201 — **[not pulled in this pass; the age-specific Canadian LTU share is the one number still to fetch]**.
- **Re-employment earnings loss after displacement (Canada):** among displaced Canadians aged 50–75 who returned to work, **almost half earned ≥25% less**, 39% about the same, 13% ≥25% more. Top self-reported barriers: "no work available" (23%), "wages too small" (21%), **"age barrier" (15%)**. Long-tenure and older workers fare worst; under-45s often lose little or gain. [StatCan 89-646-X ch.3](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/89-646-x/2010001/ch/ch3-eng.htm) (older data; still the best Canadian displacement series); [StatCan earnings losses of displaced workers](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/11f0019m/11f0019m2007291-eng.pdf); [IRPP: older displaced workers](https://irpp.org/research-studies/labour-force-participation-of-older-displaced-workers-in-canada/); [Canadian Public Policy 2017: reemployment vs early retirement vs benefits](https://utppublishing.com/doi/10.3138/cpp.2017-034)
- One-in-five displaced workers (all ages) take hourly wage cuts of 25%+ **[secondhand, via search summary of StatCan/OECD]**. [OECD Back to Work: Canada (2015)](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2015/07/back-to-work-canada_g1g52e59/9789264233454-en.pdf)

### United States (BLS / AARP)
- **Long-term unemployed share, July 2026: 23.4% of jobseekers 16–54 vs. 28.3% of jobseekers 55+.** [AARP Employment Data Digest, July 2026](https://www.aarp.org/pri/topics/work-finances-retirement/employers-workforce/employment-data-digest/); underlying BLS tables [A-36 (duration by age)](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cpseea36.htm), [A-12](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cpseea12.htm)
- **Age discrimination (AARP 2025):** 64% of workers 50+ have seen or experienced it (flat vs 2024); **37% experienced it during a job search (up from 30% in 2024)**; 22% feel pushed out because of age; stereotypes reported: "less tech-savvy" (33%), "resistant to change" (24%), younger staff preferred for training (20%). [AARP 2025 age-discrimination research](https://www.aarp.org/pri/topics/work-finances-retirement/employers-workforce/age-discrimination-workplace/); [AARP 2026 survey: pushed out](https://www.aarp.org/work/age-discrimination/age-bias-survey-2026/); [AARP Jan 2025: sharp increase in older Americans seeking a job change](https://press.aarp.org/2025-1-16-New-AARP-Survey-Sharp-Increase-Number-Older-Americans-Seeking-Job-Change)
- **Audit-study evidence of hiring discrimination:** Neumark, Burn & Button sent 40,000+ fictitious applications to 13,000+ postings in 12 cities; callbacks fall with age, worst for women and for the ~65 group; later work shows ageist language in ads correlates with lower callbacks. [BLS Monthly Labor Review summary](https://www.bls.gov/opub/mlr/2017/beyond-bls/is-there-age-discrimination-in-hiring.htm); [NBER w26552 ageist language in ads](https://www.nber.org/papers/w26552); [NBER w26623 age-blind vs age-visible](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w26623/w26623.pdf); [Implicit age cues in résumés (Frontiers 2017)](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01321/full) — implicit cues (graduation year, dated tech, "25 years of…") reduce callbacks even without a stated age.

**Takeaway for the article:** the unemployment *rate* for 55+ looks fine; the *duration* and the *re-employment pay cut* are the real risks. AI's job is to shorten duration and defend the pay level, not to spray applications.

---

## 2. What employers' AI actually does (myth vs. reality)

- **ATS ≠ auto-rejection machine.** Recruiter surveys: ~92% say the ATS does not auto-reject on content; ~90–95% of applications get human eyes at some point; the only true auto-filters are **knockout questions** (work authorization, licence, location, salary range) — 84% of recruiters use them. The real silent failure is **parsing**: columns, tables, text boxes, headers/footers and image PDFs come out scrambled or blank. A missing keyword makes you *unsearchable*, not deleted. The "75% of résumés are never seen by a human" stat is unsourced marketing. [Hiration](https://www.hiration.com/blog/ats-auto-reject-resume-myth/); [Enhancv: 25 recruiters](https://enhancv.com/blog/does-ats-reject-resumes/); [Interview Guys on the 75% myth](https://blog.theinterviewguys.com/ats-resume-rejection-myth/); [ATS myths 2026](https://atsverification.com/blog/ats-resume-myths-debunked/)
- **What is changing:** AI *ranking/scoring* layered on top of the ATS (Workday HiredScore, LinkedIn/Indeed matching, Greenhouse AI). Ranking is where age can leak in — via graduation dates, tenure length, "years of experience" fields, or dated skill vocab.
- **Application-volume inflation:** Greenhouse tracked 640M+ applications across 6,000+ companies: applications per job **rose from 116 (2022) to 244 (2025)**, a 411% rise in annual volume per recruiter while recruiting teams shrank ~55%. 77% of hiring teams regularly see AI-assisted applications (53% in early 2024); 34% of recruiters spend up to half their week filtering "AI spam." 74% of jobseekers use AI; 49% sent more applications than the prior year specifically to beat filters. Employers trust AI (70% of hiring managers) while only 8% of job seekers call it fair. [Greenhouse AI trust crisis release](https://www.greenhouse.com/newsroom/an-ai-trust-crisis-70-of-hiring-managers-trust-ai-to-make-faster-and-better-hiring-decisions-only-8-of-job-seekers-call-it-fair); [RecTech Media on Greenhouse 2026 report](https://www.rectechmedia.com/blog/2026/5/9/greenhouse-report-more-applications-fewer-recruiters); [NACE on auto-apply "ghostwritten candidates"](https://www.naceweb.org/career-readiness/best-practices/the-ghostwritten-candidate-ai-fraud-auto-apply-and-the-fight-for-authentic-career-readiness)

### Law and cases (chronological)
- **Amazon's scrapped recruiting model (2014–2017, reported 2018):** trained on 10 years of mostly-male résumés, penalized "women's" — the canonical example that a model trained on past hires reproduces past bias. Reuters, Oct 2018 **[cite from memory; verify link when writing: reuters.com "Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool"]**.
- **EEOC v. iTutorGroup (settled Aug 9, 2023):** software auto-rejected women 55+ and men 60+; $365,000 to 200+ applicants. First EEOC AI-hiring settlement — and it was an *age* case. [Sullivan & Cromwell](https://www.sullcrom.com/insights/blogs/2023/August/EEOC-Settles-First-AI-Discrimination-Lawsuit); [Akin](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/blogs/ag-data-dive/eeoc-settles-over-recruiting-software-in-possible-first-ever-ai-related-case)
- **NYC Local Law 144 (in force July 2023):** annual independent bias audit + notice for automated employment decision tools used on NYC candidates; still the only US law that mandates an audit by name. [VerityAI guide](https://verityai.co/blog/hr-ai-compliance-nyc-local-law-144-employment-law-requirements)
- **EEOC guidance rolled back (2025):** technical assistance on AI adverse impact removed from the EEOC site in early 2025; April 2025 executive order stepped back from disparate-impact enforcement; June 2025 the 2024–28 strategic enforcement plan was rescinded. Statutes (Title VII, ADEA) and the Uniform Guidelines still apply — removing guidance ≠ repealing law. [JTNY Law 2026 overview](https://jtnylaw.com/2026/04/artificial-intelligence-employment-discrimination-eeoc-hiring-algorithms/)
- **Mobley v. Workday (N.D. Cal., 3:23-cv-00770):** Derek Mobley, 40+, Black, disabled, alleges 100+ rejections via Workday-screened applications. **May 16, 2025:** preliminary collective certification on the ADEA claim (nationwide, applicants 40+ since Sept 2020). **July 7, 2025:** collective includes applicants scored/ranked/screened by HiredScore features. **Dec 2, 2025:** notice plan approved. **Mar 6, 2026:** court rejected Workday's argument that the ADEA doesn't cover applicants. **May 28, 2026:** AI bias-testing data can be shielded by attorney-client privilege. **June 22, 2026:** claims continue across age, race, sex, disability. Not resolved as of Sept 2026. [Clearinghouse docket](https://clearinghouse.net/case/44074/); [Holland & Knight on certification](https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2025/05/federal-court-allows-collective-action-lawsuit-over-alleged); [AI Governance for HR: where it stands](https://www.aigovernanceforhr.com/p/the-mobley-v-workday-case-didnt-end); [Norton Rose on the privilege ruling](https://www.insidetechlaw.com/blog/2026/06/behind-the-privilege-shield-safeguarding-ai-bias-testing-data-in-employment-decisions)
- **Ontario, Working for Workers Four Act — in force Jan 1, 2026:** employers with 25+ employees must **disclose in any public job posting if AI is used to screen, assess or select applicants**; also must state a salary range, whether the vacancy is real, may not require "Canadian experience," must retain postings 3 years, and (from 2026) tell interviewees whether a decision was made within 45 days. Enforcement is complaint-driven; no bias-audit requirement. [Osler](https://www.osler.com/en/insights/blogs/employment-and-labour-law-blog/ai-in-hiring-ontario-employers-grappling-with-new-job-posting-disclosure-requirement/); [Hicks Morley](https://hicksmorley.com/2025/12/16/new-year-new-rules-ontario-job-posting-requirements-take-effect-january-1-2026/); [HRPA](https://www.hrpa.ca/hr-insights/ontario-pay-transparency-2026/); [Workforce.com guide](https://www.workforce.com/ca/resources/ontario-job-posting-rules-2026)
  - Practical use for a reader: the disclosure line in a posting tells you whether to write for a ranking model (clean parse, exact vocabulary) or for a human first.
- **EU AI Act:** recruitment/CV screening/ranking/targeted job ads are explicitly **high-risk**; high-risk obligations apply from **Aug 2, 2026** (phased to Aug 2027): candidate notice, human oversight, bias testing, logging. Extraterritorial if outputs are used in the EU. Relevant to Canadians applying to EU-headquartered firms or global ATS deployments. [Crowell 2026 overview](https://www.crowell.com/en/insights/client-alerts/artificial-intelligence-and-human-resources-in-the-eu-a-2026-legal-overview); [DLA Piper: draft high-risk guidelines](https://knowledge.dlapiper.com/dlapiperknowledge/globalemploymentlatestdevelopments/2026/eu-commission-publishes-draft-guidelines-on-high-risk-ai-in-employment)
- Canada federally: no AI-specific hiring statute (AIDA died with Bill C-27 in Jan 2025 **[from memory]**); age is a protected ground under the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Canadian Human Rights Act regardless of whether a human or a model made the decision.

## 3. The consumer AI tool market (what it costs, what it does, what it risks)

| Tool | What it does | Price (2026) | Notes / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LinkedIn Premium Career** | AI job-fit summaries per posting, AI profile writer, message drafting, Top Applicant badge, InMail, salary/applicant insights, LinkedIn Learning | US$29.99/mo or $239.88/yr | LinkedIn claims 2.6× hire likelihood for Premium; widely disputed by users (most report getting hired free). Employer side: **Hiring Assistant** AI agent GA since Sept 2025 — recruiters review 62% fewer profiles, so the *first pass is a model* on LinkedIn-sourced hires. [Premium review](https://resumehog.com/blog/posts/linkedin-premium-career-review-2026-are-the-ai-features-worth-240.html); [Pin: Recruiter AI 2026](https://www.pin.com/blog/linkedin-recruiter-new-features/) |
| **Indeed Career Scout** (Sept 2025) | AI career coach in the app: path suggestions, résumé keywording, tailored recommendations, mock interviews; **Talent Scout** is the employer-side agent | Free | Indeed says users "find and apply 7× faster" (self-reported). [Indeed release](https://www.indeed.com/news/releases/indeed-introduces-new-suite-of-hiring-products-career-scout-talent-scout-premium-sponsored-jobs-and-indeed-connect); [What is Career Scout](https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/finding-a-job/what-is-indeed-career-scout) |
| **Teal** | Job tracker + résumé builder with per-posting keyword matching | Free tier (unlimited tracking/résumés); ~$29/mo, but priced as "$13/week" → ~$676/yr | Best value for a tracker+builder. |
| **Jobscan** | ATS keyword-match scoring per posting | 5 scans/mo free; ~$49.95/mo | Single-purpose; expensive; trains you to keyword-stuff, which recruiters dislike. |
| **Huntr** | Tracker + autofill + tailored résumés | Free: 100 tracked jobs, unlimited autofill, 2 tailored résumés; ~$40/mo | Most generous free tracker. |
| **Simplify** | Browser autofill + job matching | Free autofill; paid tier | Autofill (you click submit) is not the same as auto-apply (bot submits). |
| **Careerflow** | Résumé AI, LinkedIn optimizer, matching | Free to 15 applications; paid | |
| **Kickresume** | AI résumé builder | US$24/mo, ~$96/yr | |
| **Rezi** | AI résumé builder | $29/mo or $149 lifetime | |
| **LazyApply / Sonara / AIHawk-style auto-appliers** | Bot submits applications in bulk (Easy Apply etc.) | $99–$249+ one-off or subscription | **Violate LinkedIn User Agreement §8.2**; tiered enforcement (24–48h restriction → permanent); LazyApply on a public blacklist, 2.4/5 Trustpilot; Sonara "ignores screening questions or fills them with generic garbage." Also feeds the flood that recruiters are now filtering *against*. [Hiration verdict](https://www.hiration.com/blog/ai-auto-apply-bots/); [scale.jobs on LazyApply bans](https://scale.jobs/blog/lazyapply-risk-profile-banned-linkedin); [Resumly on Easy Apply automation risks](https://www.resumly.ai/best/best-linkedin-easy-apply-automation-tools) |

Comparison sources: [Jobscan's own roundup](https://www.jobscan.co/blog/ai-job-search-tools/); [AI Career Lab: Teal vs Huntr vs Jobscan](https://theaicareerlab.com/blog/teal-vs-huntr-vs-jobscan-vs-resumeio-2026); [BestJobSearchApps roundup](https://bestjobsearchapps.com/articles/en/7-best-aiassisted-job-search-sites-for-2026-huntr-simplify-careerflow-more). Caveat: most "comparison" sites are themselves affiliates or competitors.

**Position for the article:** a general model (ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini, or a local model) plus a free tracker does everything the paid stack does, for readers willing to write their own prompts — which is the Collegica reader.

## 4. Evidence on what works

- **Writing help raises hires — modestly.** Field experiment on an online labour market, ~480,000 jobseekers randomized to algorithmic writing assistance on their résumés: **+7.8–8% probability of being hired**, no drop in employer satisfaction; effect largest for non-native English writers. Authors argue better writing *clarifies* rather than inflates. van Inwegen, Munyikwa & Horton (2023). [arXiv 2301.08083](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08083); [MIT Sloan summary](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ideas-made-to-matter/job-seekers-ai-boosted-resumes-more-likely-to-be-hired)
- **AI cover letters raise callbacks — and then the signal decays.** Cui, Dias & Ye (Sept 2025, rev. Nov 2025): access to an AI cover-letter tool raised callback probability by 0.43 pp (+6% on baseline); implied effect on actual users ~3.6 pp (+51%). Time spent *editing* the draft predicted success. But after rollout, the correlation between letter–job textual alignment and callbacks **fell 51%** — employers stopped trusting the letter and shifted weight to **prior work history**. [arXiv 2509.25054](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25054)
  - Implication for 45–65: the one signal AI cannot fake — a long, specific work history — is the one employers are re-weighting *toward*. That is the article's core argument.
- **Recruiters vs. generic AI text:** TopResume 2026 survey of 800+ hiring managers: 67% say they can spot AI letters, 54% view them negatively; **80% reject generic AI output, 63% accept AI-assisted letters that are personalized**; 78% look for specific personal details. Tells: "proven track record," "detail-oriented professional," "I am writing to express my interest," no numbers, no company specifics. [Recruiter data on AI letters](https://coverlettercopilot.ai/blog/recruiters-human-vs-ai-cover-letters) **[secondhand; TopResume primary not fetched]**
- **Referrals dominate.** Referrals are ~7% of applicants but 30–50% of hires; referred candidates convert at ~28–34% vs 2–5% from job boards; time-to-hire ~29 vs ~44 days. Academic support: employers learn more from referrals than other channels. [SHRM](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/news/talent-acquisition/employee-referrals-remain-top-source-hires); [Labour Economics 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927537124000691); [Zippia stats roundup](https://www.zippia.com/advice/employee-referral-statistics/) (vendor-compiled; treat exact ratios as directional). The oft-quoted "85% of jobs are filled through networking" traces to a 2016 LinkedIn survey **[weak source; avoid quoting as fact]**.
- **Older-candidate specifics:** "overqualified" and salary-expectation screens act like knockout questions; implicit age cues in the résumé lower callbacks even when age isn't stated (Frontiers 2017 above). Standard mitigation advice (AARP, NCOA, Monster): drop graduation years, cap history at ~10–15 years, replace "seasoned/veteran/proven track record" with current vocabulary, lead with a skills summary, show current tools. [AARP age-proof résumé](https://www.aarp.org/work/job-search/age-proof-resume-tips/); [NCOA résumé after 50](https://www.ncoa.org/article/writing-your-resume-after-age-50-a-guide-for-older-adults/); [Monster 50+ résumé](https://www.monster.com/career-advice/article/get-your-50-plus-resume-right)

## 5. Transition paths and Canadian supports (50+)

- **Employment Insurance (regular):** 55% of average insurable weekly earnings up to **$729/week** (claims from Dec 28, 2025; MIE $68,900); **14–45 weeks** depending on hours and regional unemployment rate; you may earn while on claim (50¢ clawback per $1, up to 90% of prior weekly earnings). [Canada.ca MIE 2026](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/programs/ei/ei-list/ei-employers/premium-reduction-program/2026-maximum-insurable-earnings.html); [OSFI 2026 actuarial report](https://www.osfi-bsif.gc.ca/en/oca/actuarial-reports/2026-actuarial-report-employment-insurance-premium-rate). Training while on EI needs Service Canada/Employment Ontario approval — training-while-on-claim rules **[verify current "Section 25" referral rules before publishing]**.
- **Better Jobs Ontario (formerly Second Career):** up to **$28,000** for programs ≤1 year, **$35,000** for ≤2 years (tuition, books, transport, living allowance); eligibility broadened **Aug 20, 2025** to anyone laid off/unemployed **12+ weeks** (was 6 months) or in a low-income household; must be approved *before* training starts; guidelines updated Jan 27, 2026. [Program guidelines PDF (Jan 2026)](https://eopg.labour.gov.on.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/bjo-program-guidelines-en-2.pdf); [Sheridan how-to-apply](https://www.sheridancollege.ca/admissions/how-to-apply/better-jobs-ontario). Other provinces have analogues (BC Skills Training for Employment, Alberta Canada-Alberta Job Grant/Training for Work) **[not researched in depth]**.
- **Canada Training Credit:** refundable credit accumulating **$250/year to a $5,000 lifetime cap**, ages 26–65, claimable against eligible tuition (50% of fees up to your balance). Ends at 65 — a reason to spend it in the 50s. [CRA line 45350](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/about-your-tax-return/tax-return/completing-a-tax-return/deductions-credits-expenses/line-45350-canada-training-credit.html); [TaxTips](https://www.taxtips.ca/filing/canada-training-credit.htm)
- **AARP (US, but open):** Skills Builder for Work (300+ MindEdge courses w/ certificates, launched 2021), AARP Job Board (age-friendly employers), Small Business Resource Center for consulting/solo practice. [Skills Builder](https://www.aarp.org/work/skills-builder/); [Job board](https://jobs.aarp.org/jobs); [AARP help finding/keeping a job](https://www.aarp.org/work/careers/aarp-helps-older-workers/)
- **Fractional / consulting / portfolio work:** growing path for 50+ (fractional CFO/COO/marketing, interim roles, contract-to-hire). Fits the OWL "Go-Go" phase: income + purpose + social contact without a full-time search. Evidence on outcomes is thin/anecdotal **[no primary data found this pass]**; frame as an option with an honest "it's a sales job first" caveat.
- Bridge jobs and phased retirement are well documented in the Canadian displacement literature (older laid-off workers split between re-employment at lower pay, early CPP take-up, and EI/other benefits — [CPP 2017 paper](https://utppublishing.com/doi/10.3138/cpp.2017-034)); the OWL/Money link: taking CPP early to bridge a job gap is a permanent ~0.6%/month reduction **[from memory; confirm with Canada.ca]**.

## 6. Practical AI use-cases, with prompt patterns

Principle throughout (matching the site's existing "ratios, not identifiers" stance): the model gets *structure and drafts*; you supply *specifics and judgment*; anything identifying stays out of a hosted chat.

1. **Skills inventory from a 25-year career.** Paste a *sanitized* career timeline (roles, years, responsibilities, outcomes — no employer names if sensitive). Prompt: "Extract every transferable skill and the evidence for each. Group by: leadership, technical, domain, commercial. For each, write one line in the vocabulary a 2026 job posting would use, and one line in the vocabulary I used. Flag any skill where my evidence is >10 years old." Output → `skills-inventory.md`, versioned.
2. **Translate experience into current posting language.** Paste the posting + the inventory. "Map each requirement in this posting to my evidence. Mark: strong / partial / missing. Do not invent evidence. For 'partial', tell me what a one-paragraph story would need to show." This is a gap analysis, not a rewrite — it stops the model from confabulating.
3. **Résumé tailoring per posting (parse-safe).** "Rewrite the summary and the three most relevant bullets for this posting, in plain single-column text, no tables, using the posting's exact terms only where my evidence supports them. Keep dates on roles; remove education dates. Cap history at 15 years; summarize earlier roles in one line." Then *you* verify every claim.
4. **Cover letters that don't read as AI.** Two-step: (a) "List five specific facts about this company from the posting only." (b) "Draft 150 words that connect two of those facts to two of my stories. Ban these phrases: proven track record, detail-oriented, I am writing to express, passionate, delve, leverage." Then add one sentence only you could write (a name, a number, a place). Edit time predicts callbacks (§4).
5. **Mock interviews for the hard questions.** Role-play prompt with the posting as context: "Ask me, one at a time, and push back on vague answers: Why are you leaving? Why the gap? Why would you take a step down? Aren't you overqualified? What's your salary expectation? How current are your tools?" Record answers; ask the model to grade for specificity, not tone. Voice mode works well here for older readers who prefer talking.
6. **Salary research and negotiation.** Model as *research assistant*, not oracle: "List the public sources for this role's pay in Ontario (StatCan, Job Bank wage reports, Glassdoor, posted ranges now mandatory in Ontario postings). Build a range from posted ranges I paste." Then rehearse the negotiation as in (5). Never paste your own compensation history into a hosted model — use ratios ("current = 1.0×; target = 1.1×").
7. **LinkedIn profile rewrite.** "Rewrite my About section in first person, ≤120 words, present tense, leading with what I do now for whom, ending with what I'm looking for. No age-coded words." Keep the model out of your connection list.
8. **Informational-interview outreach.** "Draft a 60-word message to a former colleague asking for 20 minutes about how hiring works at their company now. No ask for a job. Reference one shared project: ___." Referrals convert ~10× cold applications (§4); this is the highest-value AI use for someone with a 25-year network.
9. **Privacy hygiene.** Consumer ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude train on chats **by default** unless you opt out (ChatGPT: Settings → Data Controls → "Improve the model for everyone" → off); even opted out, chats are retained ~30 days for abuse review; opt-outs are not retroactive; Team/Enterprise/API tiers have no-training terms. Redact: full name, address, SIN, employer names if under NDA, compensation figures, references' names, anything under a severance agreement. Local-model option: Ollama or LM Studio running an 8–14B model on a recent laptop handles all eight tasks above offline — slower and less polished, but nothing leaves the machine. [OpenAI privacy audit (terms.law)](https://terms.law/Privacy-Watchdog/ai-services/openai/); [TrustScan opt-out guide 2026](https://trustscan.dev/blog/opt-out-llm-training-data-2026)
10. **What AI should *not* do:** submit applications for you (bans + flood + generic answers to knockout questions), invent metrics, decide whether a step down is right for you, or replace the one phone call to a former colleague.
